target: Han köper alltid färska grönsaker från den lokala mataffären.
english: He always buys fresh vegetables from the local grocery store.
tip: 'Köpa' → 'köper' (buy): Group 2 verb – note the 'ö' is Swedish's rounded front vowel.

target: Hon tvättar kläder och städar huset varje lördag förmiddag.
english: She washes clothes and cleans the house every Saturday morning.
tip: Berry picking is a cherished tradition protected by allemansrätten.

target: Jag letar efter en bra restaurang här i närheten.
english: I am looking for a good restaurant here in the area.
tip: 'Är' (am/is/are) – same form for all persons. The most common Swedish verb.

target: Varsågod och sitt ner, kan jag bjuda dig på något?
english: Please, sit down. Can I offer you something?
tip: 'Kan' (can) stays the same for all persons – one of Swedish's simplest features.

target: Hej allihopa, jag hoppas att ni alla har det bra.
english: Hi everyone, I hope you all are doing well.
tip: Many relationship words are English loans in Swedish: singel, dejt (date), flörta (flirt).

target: Vi planerar våra måltider i förväg för att spara tid.
english: We plan our meals in advance to save time.
tip: Group 1 verbs add -r in present tense: prata → pratar.

target: Mina föräldrar bor kvar i Dalarna och jag besöker dem.
english: My parents still live in Dalarna and I visit them.
tip: You can connect clauses with "och" (and) without changing word order.

target: Han sover alltid åtta timmar per natt för sin hälsa.
english: He always sleeps eight hours per night for his health.
tip: 'Sova' → 'sover' (sleep): Group 4 irregular – present changes from -a to -er.

target: Jag drömmer om att en dag flytta ut på landet.
english: I dream of one day moving out to the countryside.
tip: Mushroom picking is a popular autumn activity, tied to allemansrätten.

target: Vi har tre barn som alla går i skolan här.
english: We have three children who all go to school here.
tip: 'Vara' (be) vs 'ha' (have) – both are essential auxiliaries. 'Är' for states, 'har' for possession and perfect tense.

target: Det är dags att vi går hem nu tror jag.
english: I think it's time we head home now.
tip: Swedish word order: the verb always comes second in main clauses, regardless of what starts the sentence.

target: Min syster och jag brukar ringa varandra varje söndag kväll.
english: My sister and I usually call each other every Sunday evening.
tip: 'Brukar' (usually do) – a uniquely Swedish verb meaning habitual action. No direct English equivalent.

target: Jag plockar svamp i skogen varje höst med min pappa.
english: I pick mushrooms in the forest every autumn with my dad.
tip: Splitting bills is the norm in Sweden, not the exception.

target: Jag undrar om du vet var biblioteket ligger i stan.
english: I wonder if you know where the library is in town.
tip: 'Veta' → 'vet' (know a fact): Irregular – 'vet' is the present form for all persons.

target: De renoverar sitt badrum och gör allt arbete helt själva.
english: They are renovating their bathroom and doing all the work themselves.
tip: 'Göra' → 'gör' (do/make): Irregular short form – no -r after the stem.

target: Jag har hört så mycket om dig från vår gemensamma vän.
english: I have heard so much about you from our mutual friend.
tip: This is the standard phrase when meeting someone for the first time.

target: Det är svårt att välja bara en favorit bland alla böcker.
english: It is hard to choose just one favorite among all books.
tip: "Ha" is irregular: har (present), hade (past), haft (supine).

target: Jag äter havregrynsgröt.
english: I eat oatmeal porridge.
tip: Havregrynsgröt is a classic Swedish breakfast, often with milk and jam.

target: Det finns laddstolpar för elbilar.
english: There are charging stations for electric cars.
tip: Sweden is rapidly expanding its electric car infrastructure.

target: Du skämtar väl inte med mig om det här?
english: You are surely not joking with me about this?
tip: Subordinating conjunctions don't push the verb to the very end (that's German). But they DO flip the inte/verb order. Main: `verb + inte`. Sub: `inte + verb`.

target: Jag är hungrig.
english: I am hungry.
tip: Swedish present tense is simple: one form for all persons. Just add -r to the verb stem.

target: Vi åker spårvagn.
english: We take the tram.
tip: "Spårvagn" = tram. Gothenburg is famous for its tram network – stockholm doesn't have trams.

target: Kaffet är varmt.
english: The coffee is hot.
tip: "Varm" → "varmt" for ett-words. The -t makes it neuter.

target: Hon går till jobbet.
english: She walks to work.
tip: 'Gå' → 'går' (go/walk): Group 3 short verb – just add -r to the infinitive.

target: Det är kallt ute.
english: It is cold outside.
tip: Swedish has two genders: en (common, ~75%) and ett (neuter, ~25%). The article attaches as a suffix for 'the'.

target: Jag har tre barn.
english: I have three children.
tip: "Barn" is an ett-word that stays the same in plural: ett barn, två barn.

target: Där borta ligger affären.
english: Over there lies the store.
tip: "Där borta" = over there. Place adverb first → verb second → subject third.

target: Vi förbereder oss för vintern.
english: We prepare ourselves for winter.
tip: Swedish verbs don't change with person: "jag talar", "du talar", "han talar".

target: Vi hade en trevlig kväll.
english: We had a pleasant evening.
tip: "Ha" → "hade" in past tense. Irregular but very common.

target: Hon tror att det blir regn här.
english: She thinks it will rain here.
tip: 'Tro' → 'tror' (believe): Group 3 short verb – add -r to the infinitive.

target: Hon städar huset på fredagar.
english: She cleans the house on Fridays.
tip: This is a group 1 (-ar) verb – regular and predictable. Past tense adds -ade: 'tittar' → 'tittade'.

target: Vi sitter i tyst avdelning.
english: We sit in the quiet car.
tip: Swedish trains have "tyst avdelning" (quiet sections) where phone calls are not allowed.

target: Hon lär ha berättat hemligheten.
english: She is said to have told the secret.
tip: "Lär ha" = is said to have – another way to report unconfirmed information.

target: Det är fem minuters promenad härifrån.
english: It's a five-minute walk from here.
tip: "Härifrån" = from here. Compound: här+i+från. Swedish loves building words this way.

target: Ursäkta, vet du var biblioteket ligger?
english: Excuse me, do you know where the library is?
tip: 'Var' (where) – for location questions: 'Var bor du?' (Where do you live?).

target: De har två hundar och en katt.
english: They have two dogs and a cat.
tip: Group 1 verbs (most common) form past with "-ade": "tala" → "talade".

target: Hon övar piano i minst en timme.
english: She practices piano for at least one hour.
tip: Swedish question words: vad, var, vem, när, hur, varför, vilken – the verb always follows immediately.

target: God morgon, vad ska du göra idag?
english: Good morning, what are you going to do today?
tip: 'Vad' (what) – starts questions: 'Vad gör du?' (What do you do?). Verb comes right after.

target: Har ni veganskt alternativ just nu väl?
english: Do you have a vegan option right now I suppose?
tip: Swedish loves compound nouns – long words made of smaller ones. `Tandborste` = tooth + brush. Break them apart to read: `tand` + `borste`. The last piece carries the gender.

target: God kväll, är den här platsen ledig bredvid dig?
english: Good evening, is this seat free next to you?
tip: Swedish questions: use a question word + verb, or invert subject and verb for yes/no questions.

target: Vi besöker museer och gallerier när vi har ledigt.
english: We visit museums and galleries when we have time off.
tip: Sweden is one of the world's most cashless societies – card or Swish for most transactions.

target: Han ritar skisser av byggnader han ser ute i staden.
english: He draws sketches of buildings he sees around the city.
tip: 'Se' → 'ser' (see): Group 3 short verb – just add -r.

target: Det är svårt att hitta en bra lägenhet i Stockholm.
english: It is hard to find a good apartment in Stockholm.
tip: Swedish simplifies be/have: 'är' (am/is/are) and 'har' (have/has) – no person agreement needed.

target: Jag har en kompis som arbetar på en ambassad utomlands.
english: I have a friend who works at an embassy abroad.
tip: July is the main vacation month. Many businesses slow down or close.

target: De reser ofta till andra länder under sommarlovet varje år.
english: They often travel to other countries during summer vacation every year.
tip: Cycling is the primary transport for many Swedes, especially in Malmö and Uppsala.

target: Fäktaren parerade motståndarens attack med precision.
english: The fencer parried the opponent's attack with precision.
tip: Having a "stuga" (cottage) is a Swedish dream. Many families have one.

target: Vakna.
english: Wake up.
tip: Starting a sentence with a non-subject element creates an inversion: the verb stays second and the subject follows it directly.

target: Vänta lite.
english: Wait a moment.
tip: Notice how the verb stays in second position even when time or place comes first. This V2 pattern is automatic for native speakers.

target: En miljon invånare.
english: One million inhabitants.
tip: "Miljon" is an en-word: en miljon, miljonen. "Invånare" = inhabitant – same singular and plural.

target: Barnet är litet.
english: The child is small.
tip: Swedish V2 order feels natural once you internalize it: the verb is the anchor at position two, everything else arranges around it.

target: Det är varmt ute.
english: It is warm outside.
tip: `Det är` doesn't care about gender or number of what follows: `det är en bok`, `det är böcker`. Always `det är` in front, regardless.

target: Vi behöver tolv ägg.
english: We need twelve eggs.
tip: "Ägg" is ett-word: ett ägg, ägget. Same form singular and plural.

target: Ta buss nummer sju.
english: Take bus number seven.
tip: Transport: ta bussen (take the bus), åka tåg (go by train), flyga (fly). No article after 'nummer.'

target: Idag äter vi pasta.
english: Today we eat pasta.
tip: V2 rule: the verb must be second. When a non-subject starts, the subject moves after the verb.

target: Jag läser en bok.
english: I read a book.
tip: Standard SVO order when subject starts – no inversion needed.

target: Nu börjar det regna.
english: Now it's starting to rain.
tip: "Nu" at front triggers V2: Nu + börjar + det (subject after verb).

target: Barnen väcks klockan sju.
english: The children are woken at seven o'clock.
tip: In Swedish main clauses, the verb is always in second position – even when the sentence starts with a time expression or adverb.

target: Hon har nyligen kommit tillbaka.
english: She has recently come back.
tip: "Nyligen" = recently. Goes between "har" and the supine.

target: Jag köpte en ny bil.
english: I bought a new car.
tip: "Bil" is en-word: en bil, bilen, bilar, bilarna.

target: Igår regnade det hela dagen.
english: Yesterday it rained all day.
tip: "Igår" first → "regnade" second → "det" third. This is V2 inversion.
